title: Tideway Manufacturing POC — Concurrency & Cost Sensitivity Benchmark
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures the benchmarking campaign run for Tideway Manufacturing's POC focused on concurrency and cost sensitivity for an LLM-based production assistant used on the factory floor. Goal: quantify latency tail behavior, sustainable throughput at target SLAs, and token cost trade-offs for different model/quantization configurations so Tideway can choose a deployment profile for their pilot.

Key takeaways (short):
- Baseline (MistralX-7B fp16) meets p95 < 250ms at concurrency <= 10 for short prompts (avg 120 tokens) with cost ~ $1.8 / 1000 responses.
- Larger model (Llama-3-70B q4) gives better instruction-following but p95 rises rapidly beyond concurrency 3; requires batching or dedicated pools to be cost-viable.
- Quantized medium model (Mistral-7B q4f16) gives ~1.6x token throughput improvement vs fp16 and reduces cost by ~35% with minimal quality loss on Tideway prompts.
- Recommendation: start pilot on Mistral-7B q4f16 with 2 dedicated GPUs (reserved) and autoscale burst to hosted capacity for peak shifts.

Scope and success criteria:
- Workloads: short-form operator chat (avg 120 tokens), ticket summarization (avg 600 tokens), and embeddings for search (128-d vector flow).
- SLA targets agreed with Tideway: p95 latency <= 350ms for chat, p95 <= 1.5s for summarization. Cost target: <$2.5 per 1000 chat responses at pilot volumes.
- Tests run simulate steady-state plus burst patterns (10m ramp, 30m steady, 5m peak bursts).

Test environment and configuration:
- Date range: 2026-12-08 to 2026-12-12 (engineering lab).
- Hardware: AWS g5.12xlarge (4 × A10G), and dedicated on-prem node (NVIDIA H100 PCIe) for high-capacity runs.
- Redwood runtime: engine v2.9.1 with continuous-batching enabled, prefix caching disabled for deterministic measurements.
- Models tested: Mistral-7B (fp16), Mistral-7B (q4f16), Llama-3-70B (q4), Llama-3-70B (fp16, on H100).
- Tokenization: byte-level BPE; test prompts derived from anonymized Tideway transcripts (N=12k samples).

Workload characterization:
- Chat operator: 70% short queries (avg 90–150 tokens), 30% follow-ups (avg 220 tokens) — latency-critical.
- Summarization: single-shot product incident transcripts, 450–900 tokens input, output 80–160 tokens — throughput-focused but lenient latency.
- Embedding pipeline: batched requests, target throughput 200 qps during batch windows.

Test matrix (representative):
- Concurrency sweep (1, 3, 5, 10, 20, 40) at fixed prompt mix for chat (avg 120 tokens).
- Sequence length sweep for summarization (input 450, 600, 900).
- Model/config comparisons for identical concurrency points.
- Burst profiles: 100->400 concurrent over 60s to observe cold-start/fallback behavior.

Measurement methodology:
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (server-side), tokens/sec (aggregate), qps, GPU util, cost estimate (tokenized cost using Redwood pricing for reserved vs hosted).
- Each measurement window: 30 minutes steady-state after warm-up of 10 minutes.
- Error handling: requests with >5% server errors flagged and root-caused (OOM, model load, rate limit).

Results (selected highlights):
1) Chat workload (avg 120 tokens) — AWS g5 (A10G)
- Mistral-7B fp16:
  - concurrency 1: p50=45ms, p95=120ms, throughput=95 qps, cost est= $0.0020/response
  - concurrency 10: p50=200ms, p95=320ms, throughput=720 qps (aggregate), cost est= $0.0019/response
  - concurrency 40: p95 spikes to ~1.1s, CPU scheduling overhead noticeable; GPU util 78%
- Mistral-7B q4f16:
  - concurrency 1: p95=95ms, throughput=150 qps, cost est= $0.0014/response
  - concurrency 10: p95=210ms, throughput=1100 qps, cost est= $0.0012/response
  - concurrency 40: p95=430ms, throughput gains tail off due to driver bottleneck
- Llama-3-70B q4 (on same A10G cluster):
  - concurrency 1: p95=240ms, throughput=30 qps, cost est= $0.0058/response
  - concurrency 3: p95=480ms (beyond SLA), throughput=75 qps
  - H100 (fp16) for 70B: concurrency 1 p95=120ms, throughput=80 qps but infra cost + higher reserved pricing increases per-response cost to ~$0.007

Interpretation: medium model quantized (q4f16) offers the best cost/throughput balance for chat; large model only justified where instruction quality improvement is essential for use cases.

2) Summarization workload (avg 600 tokens output ~120 tokens) — H100 and A10G comparative:
- Mistral-7B q4f16 on g5: p95 ~1.2s at concurrency 5, throughput ~40 summaries/min per node.
- Llama-3-70B fp16 on H100: p95 ~900ms at concurrency 3, throughput ~65 summaries/min but cost per summary 2.5x.

3) Embeddings pipeline:
- Batched embeddings (batch size 64) using embedding model X (small, optimized) reached 1800 vectors/sec on A10G farm; cost within Tideway budget for nightly indexing.

Cost sensitivity and sizing examples (pilot volumes):
- Tideway expected pilot volume: 250k chat responses/day.
- Mistral-7B q4f16 reserve config (2 × g5 nodes) + 20% burst to hosted: estimated monthly infra + tokens cost = $14k (within customer budget).
- Llama-3-70B dedicated on H100 (1 node) estimate = $36k/month due to lower throughput and higher GPU amortization.

Stability and failure modes observed:
- Model load times: q4 variants load faster (~6–8s) versus fp16 70B (~45–60s) when warming new worker process. Plan for preloading on pool scale-up.
- Tail latency correlates tightly with system-level GPU context switches under high concurrency — driver tuning (NVIDIA persistence mode, CUDA mempool) improved p95 by ~18% in follow-up trials.
- Occasional 502s at extreme bursts traced to upstream queue backlog; mitigated by applying backpressure at route and queue depth limit of 500.

Quality checks (quick):
- Automated eval on 2k representative prompts: Mistral-7B q4f16 BLEU/ROUGE drops <2% vs fp16 baseline on operational metrics; human review found acceptable answers for 94% of cases.
- Llama-3-70B produced slightly more verbose procedural outputs; for Tideway this was judged marginally superior on 10% of prompts (safety acceptable).

Recommendations (practical roadmap):
1) Pilot configuration (0–3 months):
   - Use Mistral-7B q4f16 as default for chat; provision 2 reserved g5.12xlarge nodes, enable continuous-batching at conservative batch windows (max 20ms) and set concurrency cap of 20 per node.
   - Configure autoscale policy: scheduled scale-in overnight, burst to hosted API when sustained queue >2000 requests.
   - Preload workers on scale-up events; enable persistence mode on GPUs.
2) Monitoring & SLOs:
   - Add model-level dashboards in Redwood Console: tokens/s, p95, GPU mem pressure, model load time.
   - Create synthetic canary every 60s with representative short prompt to detect tail regressions.
3) If higher LLM quality needed:
   - Evaluate Llama-3-70B on H100 in a separate quality track; only enable for routes labeled "high-quality" with strict quota.

Action items and next steps:
- SE to produce cost model spreadsheet for Tideway (linked) with 3 adoption scenarios (conservative, likely, aggressive) — owner: Arjun (due 2026-12-20).
- DevOps to apply GPU driver tuning playbook to pilot nodes and test persistence mode — owner: Liam (due 2026-12-17).
- Run 72-hour soak using pilot config and collect telemetry for production sign-off — owner: Sofia (start 2026-12-18).

Appendix (raw numbers table pointers):
- See attached run logs in GitHub run artifacts (linked_artifacts above) and the CSV dump in Confluence page CONFLUENCE-1204.
- Quick reproducibility: scripts/run_tideway_sweep.sh in the repo will recreate core comparatives; PR 42 contains the exact params used.

Notes to reviewer:
- This is a working benchmarking report (in_review). Some long-run soak data pending; numbers in the executive summary are the most stable across repeated runs.
- Questions: if Tideway wants per-route custom quantization (mix q4f16 for chat, fp16 for summarization) we should plan rolling rollout and A/B evals to confirm end-to-end UX impact.

End of document.
